[2026-15665: lines 2137-2536 of 6220, FR page 49195]
  2137  C. Part 351, Subpart D: Changes in How Competitive Areas Are Defined 
  2138  and Approved
  2139  
  2140      This rule revises Sec.  351.402(b) to allow agencies to designate a 
  2141  competitive area as being any organizational unit, or combination of 
  2142  organizational units, on an agency's official organizational chart. 
  2143  Organizational charts must be available on the agency's public facing 
  2144  web page or otherwise appropriately documented by the agency. An 
  2145  organizational unit for these purposes must be designated/approved by 
  2146  the head of the agency, or designee, and the designation or approval 
  2147  cannot be redelegated to an official below the agency's headquarters 
  2148  level.
  2149      In addition, OPM is revising Sec.  351.402(b) to require that an 
  2150  organizational unit for purposes of a RIF must be clearly distinguished 
  2151  from other organizational units with regard to its operation, work 
  2152  function, staff, and supervisory oversight. In addition, OPM is 
  2153  clarifying that field or regional offices officially established by the 
  2154  agency as discrete organizational units and shown on the agency's 
  2155  official organizational chart may be their own competitive area(s).
  2156      Commenter 0684 contended that the previous regulatory phrase 
  2157  ``under separate administration'' was not vague but had an accepted 
  2158  meaning as encompassing ``the authority to take or direct personnel 
  2159  actions.'' Commenter 0684 argued that the requirement in this rule that 
  2160  an organizational unit be differentiated from other organizational 
  2161  units with regard to its operation, work function, staff, and 
  2162  supervisory oversight is not equivalent to the previous phrase.
  2163      However, the previous OPM rulemaking and Federal Circuit case cited 
  2164  by Commenter 0684 state that ``under separate administration'' may be 
  2165  satisfied by as little as the authority to ``assign duties,'' a power 
  2166  that any front-line supervisor would possess. Further, OPM's current 
  2167  Workforce Reshaping Operations Handbook rejects Commenter 0684's 
  2168  definition of ``under separate administration,'' as OPM states that the 
  2169  definition ``[r]ecognizes that individual organizational components may 
  2170  be under separate administration even though many agencies reserve 
  2171  final approval of certain personnel actions to a higher level in the 
  2172  agency.'' \15\ Ultimately, Commenter 0684 only underscores that the 
  2173  phrase ``under separate administration'' is confusing, and that OPM was 
  2174  correct in the proposed rule in stating that ``the current terminology 
  2175  is not aligned with the operational realities of Federal agencies, 
  2176  where many components may be `under separate administration' in some 
  2177  important respects, but under centralized administration in other 
  2178  important respects.''
  2179  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2180  
  2181      \15\ OPM, Workforce Reshaping Operations Handbook, at pp. 30-31, 
  2182  https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/reductions-in-force-rif/workforce_reshaping.pdf.
  2183  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2184  
  2185      Commenter 0684 also contended that Sec.  351.402(b) ``no longer 
  2186  specifies that the definition is the minimum competitive area, and thus 
  2187  strips agencies of the flexibility to expand a small competitive area 
  2188  to allow for competition.'' But that is not so: section 351.402(b) 
  2189  continues to state that a ``competitive area may consist of any 
  2190  organizational unit or combination of units established on the agency's 
  2191  official organizational chart,'' which allows agencies to expand a 
  2192  small competitive area to allow for greater competition.
  2193      Commenter 0687 expressed appreciation that ``OPM is taking 
  2194  competitive area manipulation seriously and agree[d] with OPM's stated 
  2195  intent to preserve rules against it,'' but presented several issues 
  2196  with OPM's new proposed definition. The commenter noted that Federal 
  2197  agencies are not required to maintain a single ``official'' 
  2198  organizational chart, and in practice agencies or their subparts may 
  2199  maintain several organizational charts for different purposes, which 
  2200  may not reflect how the agency manages itself on a day-to-day basis. 
  2201  Therefore, Commenter 0687 suggested that OPM
  2202  
  2203  [[Page 49196]]
  2204  
  2205  ``pick a single, authoritative dataset for the purposes of competitive 
  2206  area definition: the hierarchy utilized during administration of the 
  2207  Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey [FEVS] in the most immediately prior 
  2208  year.''
  2209      OPM appreciates Commenter 0687's suggestion but does not adopt it. 
  2210  OPM believes that administration of FEVS should remain flexible and 
  2211  responsive to agency needs and not be tied to administration of RIFs. 
  2212  OPM also believes that agencies may reasonably adopt new organizational 
  2213  charts that deviate from the structure reflected in their previous 
  2214  year's administration of FEVS based on evolving mission needs, 
  2215  including changes in agency budgets, technology, and presidential and 
  2216  congressional priorities. Indeed, the RIF regulations have long applied 
  2217  where release is required due to, inter alia, ``reorganization,'' see 5 
  2218  CFR 351.201(a)(2), defined as ``the planned elimination, addition, or 
  2219  redistribution of functions or duties in an organization,'' see 5 CFR 
  2220  351.203. OPM believes that the limitations in Sec.  351.402(c) against 
  2221  recognizing new competitive areas that will be in effect for less than 
  2222  90 days before issuance of RIF notices, as augmented by changes 
  2223  described below, provide sufficient guardrails against competitive area 
  2224  manipulation.
  2225      Commenter 0683 also expressed concern about the ``potential for 
  2226  gerrymandering competitive areas to target particular employees or 
  2227  groups of employees.'' It suggested that ``OPM require agencies to 
  2228  establish competitive area designations through a transparent process, 
  2229  with documentation available for review, and to prohibit agencies from 
  2230  establishing or modifying competitive areas after a decision to conduct 
  2231  a RIF has been made.''
  2232      OPM agrees with this suggestion, in part. In this final rule, OPM 
  2233  is adding an additional safeguard against competitive area 
  2234  manipulation: when agencies are seeking approval from OPM for a new 
  2235  competitive area that has existed for less than 90 days prior to 
  2236  issuing specific RIF notices, the agency shall submit a description of 
  2237  the competitive area, along with a written statement explaining the 
  2238  bona fide organizational basis for the competitive area, to OPM for 
  2239  approval in advance of the RIF. Such approval is also required where an 
  2240  agency materially modifies a competitive area. In addition, 
  2241  descriptions of all competitive areas, and accompanying explanations 
  2242  submitted to OPM, must be made readily available for review consistent 
  2243  with national security considerations and applicable laws including the 
  2244  Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552), and the Privacy Act (5 
  2245  U.S.C. 552a). In addition, as noted above, OPM is requiring expressly 
  2246  that the RIF regulations be administered consistent with the merit 
  2247  system principles set forth in 5 U.S.C. 2301. OPM believes that these 
  2248  suggestions adequately address the concerns expressed by Commenters 
  2249  0683 and 0687 regarding competitive area manipulation. These further 
  2250  advance Commenter 0685's call for OPM to ``strengthen requirements 
  2251  related to transparency and documentation'' in the final rule.
  2252  
  2253  D. Part 351, Subpart E: New Method of Deriving Retention Standing, 
  2254  Revised Order of Retention Examples, and Additional Examples
  2255  
  2256      OPM is finalizing its changes to 5 CFR part 351, subpart E 
  2257  ``Retention Standing,'' including revised and reorganized content in 
  2258  Sec. Sec.  351.501 through 351.504. In addition, OPM is renumbering 
  2259  current Sec.  351.505 Records and Sec.  351.506 Effective date of 
  2260  retention standing to Sec.  351.506 Records and Sec.  351.507 Effective 
  2261  date of retention standing, respectively.
  2262      As noted above, under this rule (and particularly Sec.  351.501 
  2263  Order of retention), when determining the order in which employees are 
  2264  placed on a RIF retention register, agencies will now do so based on 
  2265  whether the employee is in the competitive service tenure group or 
  2266  excepted service tenure group. Within each group, employees will be 
  2267  ranked based on performance, as augmented by additional points for 
  2268  veterans' preference. Where employees are tied, the employee in the 
  2269  higher tenure subgroup (with subgroup I ranked ahead of subgroup II) 
  2270  will be ranked ahead. When employees are still tied, the employee with 
  2271  the longer service will be ranked ahead.
  2272      In Sec.  351.502 Tenure of employment, OPM is redefining the tenure 
  2273  groups for both the competitive and excepted services. The competitive 
  2274  service tenure group will consist of all competitive service employees 
  2275  (in accordance with the provisions of Sec.  315.201) who are not (as of 
  2276  the date of the RIF notice) serving an initial probationary period or a 
  2277  temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under 5 CFR 
  2278  part 316. The excepted service tenure group will consist of excepted 
  2279  service employees occupying a career position (as defined in Sec.  
  2280  213.101) who are not serving a trial period and are not serving in a 
  2281  temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less.
  2282      In addition, competitive service tenure subgroup I will include 
  2283  each career employee in the competitive service who, as of the date the 
  2284  employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, is not serving 
  2285  an initial probationary period. This definition is substantially the 
  2286  same as the current competitive service tenure group I.
  2287      Competitive service tenure subgroup II will consist of every other 
  2288  competitive service employee who, as of the date of the RIF notice, is 
  2289  not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or term 
  2290  appointment of 1 year or less. For example, an employee serving under a 
  2291  career-conditional competitive service appointment who has completed a 
  2292  probationary period but not yet completed the service requirements for 
  2293  career tenure (under 5 CFR 315.201) would be included in subgroup II.
  2294      Excepted service tenure subgroup I will include all employees 
  2295  occupying a career position (that is to say, not in Schedule C or G) in 
  2296  the excepted service who, as of the date the employee receives a 
  2297  specific reduction in force notice, are not serving a trial period and 
  2298  whose appointment carries no restriction or condition such as 
  2299  conditional, indefinite, or specific time limit. This definition is 
  2300  substantially the same as current excepted service tenure group I.
  2301      Excepted service tenure subgroup II will consist of all other 
  2302  career employees in the excepted service (that is to say, not in 
  2303  Schedule C or G) who are not serving a trial period or a temporary or 
  2304  time-limited appointment of 1 year or less. Examples of employees in 
  2305  excepted service tenure subgroup II include employees occupying career 
  2306  positions in the excepted service who have completed any required trial 
  2307  period and who are serving under conditional, indefinite, or specific 
  2308  time-limited appointments of more than 1 year.
  2309      OPM revises Sec.  351.503 Performance to state that an agency will 
  2310  list employees on a RIF retention register (within the same tenure 
  2311  group) based on each employee's calculated performance credit. 
  2312  Generally, the three most recent ratings of record received during the 
  2313  4-year period prior to the date of issuance of reduction in force 
  2314  notices may be considered; however, an agency may establish a cut-off 
  2315  date after which no new rating of record will be considered. Ratings of 
  2316  record will be assigned a numerical value in conjunction with the 
  2317  patterns of summary level in 5 CFR 430.208(e) as follows:
  2318  
  2319  [[Page 49197]]
  2320  
  2321  
  2322  
  2323  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2324                                                            Performance
  2325           Summary level            Rating description         credit
  2326  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2327  Level 5.......................  Outstanding or                         7
  2328                                   equivalent.
  2329  Level 4.......................  Exceeds Fully                          5
  2330                                   Successful or
  2331                                   equivalent.
  2332  Level 3.......................  Fully Successful or                    3
  2333                                   equivalent.
  2334  Level 2.......................  Minimally                              0
  2335                                   Satisfactory or
  2336                                   equivalent.
  2337  Level 1.......................  Unacceptable.........                  0
  2338  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2339  
  2340      Agencies will list competing employees on the retention register in 
  2341  descending order (within the same tenure group) based on each 
  2342  employee's performance credit, which is the sum of the values assigned 
  2343  for their three most recent ratings of record received during the 4-
  2344  year period prior to the issuance of RIF notices. Employees would then 
  2345  receive additional performance credit based on veteran status: each 
  2346  preference eligible veteran with a compensable service-connected 
  2347  disability of 30 percent or more receives an additional 5 points added 
  2348  to their total performance credit, while every other preference 
  2349  eligible veteran would then receive an additional 3 points added to 
  2350  their total performance credit.
  2351      For example, the employees below are covered under a pattern C 
  2352  four-summary level rating performance appraisal system as described in 
  2353  5 CFR 430.208(e). Their ratings and totals are:
  2354  
  2355  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2356                                                                                      Performance
  2357                              Employee                                  Ratings         credit           Total
  2358  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2359  Alice...........................................................           5/4/4           7/5/5              17
  2360  Bill............................................................           4/3/3           5/3/3              11
  2361  Carol...........................................................           4/4/3           5/5/3              13
  2362  Fred............................................................           3/4/5           3/5/7              15
  2363  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2364  
  2365      These employees would be listed on the retention register in the 
  2366  following order: Alice, Fred, Carol, then Bill.
  2367      Section 351.503(b) Ratings used establishes which ratings of record 
  2368  may be used as the basis for calculating an employee's performance 
  2369  credit. For most employees, an employee's ratings of record are those 
  2370  recorded pursuant to subpart B of 5 CFR part 430.
  2371      Section 351.503(c) Consideration of performance includes language 
  2372  currently in Sec.  351.504(b) but modifies this language by removing 
  2373  the reference to ``additional retention service credit'' (i.e., credit 
  2374  for performance will no longer be added to an employee's length of 
  2375  service). Performance will now be the primary basis for rating 
  2376  employees within each tenure group. Performance will be measured based 
  2377  on performance credit, i.e., the total of each employee's summary level 
  2378  ratings for the employee's three most recent ratings of record for 
  2379  performance consistent with Sec.  351.503(a), which will then be 
  2380  augmented by additional credit for veterans' preference status as set 
  2381  forth in Sec.  351.504.
  2382      New paragraph Sec.  351.503(d) Single rating pattern describes how 
  2383  agencies list employees who have been covered under the same rating 
  2384  pattern of summary levels during the 4-year period prior to the date of 
  2385  issuance of the reduction in force notice or the agency-established 
  2386  cutoff date. Paragraph (d) provides that, for employees covered under a 
  2387  summary level appraisal system in which the highest summary level is a 
  2388  level ``3'' rating (i.e., a pattern A (`pass/fail'), or pattern D 
  2389  system authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed 
  2390  at 91 FR 41521), the agency may, in its sole and exclusive discretion, 
  2391  give additional credit for employees who have documented exceptional 
  2392  performance to give more weight to certain performance-related actions 
  2393  than others for purposes of listing some level ``3'' employees ahead of 
  2394  other employees on a retention register. Evidence of exceptional 
  2395  performance may include documentation showing an agency has awarded: an 
  2396  employee with the highest Agency or Departmental award (such as a 
  2397  Secretary's or Chairman's award), a special act or service award, a 
  2398  quality step increase (QSI), or other performance awards or bonuses 
  2399  (e.g., a ``time-off'' award for demonstrated performance above 
  2400  expectations).
  2401      Commenter 0683 expressed concern that this could ``create[] a 
  2402  system in which the same level of actual performance could yield 
  2403  materially different retention outcomes depending on which agency the 
  2404  employee works for and what award budget was available.'' OPM 
  2405  disagrees. Instead, it believes this change will provide a method by 
  2406  which an agency may make meaningful distinctions among employees in a 
  2407  pattern A performance appraisal program (i.e., the highest summary 
  2408  level rating is a ``3'' or satisfactory) who have documented 
  2409  performance above expectations in these appraisal systems. It thus 
  2410  directly addresses Commenter 0683's concern that existing performance 
  2411  appraisal systems do not always meaningfully differentiate relative 
  2412  performance, along with Commenter 0683's concerns regarding variations 
  2413  in rating patterns across agencies.
  2414      For example, the employees below are covered under a three-summary 
  2415  level pattern as described in 5 CFR 430.208(e). Their agency has an 
  2416  established policy of providing enhanced performance credit by 
  2417  assigning 7 points for agency awards, 5 points for organizational 
  2418  awards, and 4 points for various performance awards. (An agency award 
  2419  is designated by ``A''; a component-level award is designated by ``O''; 
  2420  and a performance award or QSI is designated by ``P''.) Their ratings 
  2421  and totals are:
  2422  
  2423  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2424                                                                                    Assigned
  2425            Employee                Ratings       Performance       Award(s)       values for          Total
  2426                                                    credit                           awards
  2427  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2428  Carol.......................           3/3/3           3/3/3  O/O/A..........           5/5/7     3+3+3+5+5+7=26
  2429  Alice.......................           3/3/3           3/3/3  A/-/P..........           7/0/4       3+3+3+7+4=20
  2430  Bill........................           2/3/3           0/3/3  -/-/P..........           0/0/4     0+3+3+0+0+4=10
  2431  
  2432  [[Page 49198]]
  2433  
  2434   
  2435  Fred........................           3/3/3           3/3/3  -/-/-..........           0/0/0      3+3+3+0+0+0=9
  2436  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2437  
  2438      New paragraph Sec.  351.503(e) Multiple rating patterns addresses 
  2439  situations in which an agency has employees in a competitive area who 
  2440  have ratings of record under more than one pattern of summary levels, 
  2441  as described in 5 CFR 430.208(e). An agency may, in its sole and 
  2442  exclusive discretion, choose to provide enhanced performance credit to 
  2443  employees under disparate pattern summary levels. It may do so by 
  2444  transmuting or assigning an employee a higher summary level rating than 
  2445  what he or she received under a previous rating system when there is 
  2446  documented evidence of exceptional or higher-level performance 
  2447  consistent with the criteria in revised Sec.  351.503(d).
  2448      In addition, for an employee who goes from an appraisal system 
  2449  which uses a higher pattern of summary levels to a lower one (e.g., an 
  2450  employee who goes from a 5 summary level appraisal program to a two 
  2451  level system (i.e., pass/fail system)), an agency may adopt policies 
  2452  which would allow employees with ratings above the highest summary 
  2453  level of the lower pattern system to be listed ahead of any employee on 
  2454  the retention register who does not have documented evidence of 
  2455  exceptional performance as described above. This method allows agencies 
  2456  to adopt policies that would prevent exceptional performers from being 
  2457  disadvantaged because they may be covered under two or more patterns of 
  2458  summary rating levels which may not make meaningful distinctions for 
  2459  performance among employees. Further, Sec.  351.503 will require RIF 
  2460  performance ratings and assigned summary levels, including adjustments, 
  2461  to be uniformly and consistently applied within the competitive area 
  2462  and consistent with the agency's implementing issuances. Where an 
  2463  agency elects to assign additional performance credit, the agency must 
  2464  specify and document the criteria in advance and make them available 
  2465  for review.
  2466      Paragraph (f) of Sec.  351.503 describes how an agency should 
  2467  factor performance ratings into the RIF process when an employee does 
  2468  not have three actual ratings of record during the 4-year period prior 
  2469  to the date of issuance of RIF notices, or the 4-year period prior to 
  2470  the agency-established cut-off date. It uses the modal rating concept 
  2471  for employees with no ratings during the 4-year period prior to the 
  2472  RIF, as currently found in Sec.  351.504(c)(1), but modifies the 
  2473  current provisions by removing the reference to ``additional retention 
  2474  service credit.''
  2475      Section 351.504 Veterans' preference defines how veterans' 
  2476  preference will be applied in a RIF in both the competitive and 
  2477  excepted services. Each preference eligible employee with a compensable 
  2478  service-connected disability of 30 percent or more will receive an 
  2479  additional 5 points added to their performance credit, while every 
  2480  other preference eligible employee will receive an additional 3 points 
  2481  added to their performance credit. ``Preference eligibles'' is defined 
  2482  in 5 U.S.C. 2108(3) to include not only veterans, but also certain 
  2483  close family members of deceased or service-disabled veterans. Non-
  2484  preference eligible employees do not receive any additional points 
  2485  added to their performance score.
  2486      Commenter 0660 asserted, without any additional information, that 
  2487  ``the proposed rules are vague and unclear as to exactly how 
  2488  performance and veterans' issues are to be determined,'' but does not 
  2489  indicate in what manner the proposed rule is vague or unclear, 
  2490  providing no supporting information whatsoever. Commenter 0660 
  2491  contended that ``[t]he proposed regulation will make it likely that the 
  2492  classifications will result in numerous appeals challenging the order 
  2493  and create chaos in their implementation as a result,'' but failed to 
  2494  explain how the new regulation is more complicated than the current 
  2495  rules.
  2496      OPM disagrees with Commenter 0660's assertions. The current rules 
  2497  require agencies to categorize employees based on tenure group and 
  2498  veterans' preference subgroup. Employees are ranked first by tenure 
  2499  group I, II, III; then within each tenure group by veterans' preference 
  2500  subgroup AD, A, B; and only then by years of service as augmented by 
  2501  performance credit, starting with the earliest service date. Agencies 
  2502  then prepare an ``adjusted SCD'' calculation where extra years of 
  2503  service are added to an employee's actual service computation date. 
  2504  That means current RIF ordering is not a simple comparison of Employee 
  2505  A's performance against Employee B's performance. Agencies must first 
  2506  place employees into tenure groups, then veterans' preference 
  2507  subgroups, then calculate adjusted service dates. Performance affects 
  2508  ranking only inside the employee's already-determined tenure/veterans' 
  2509  preference category.
  2510      Agencies then must undergo multiple rounds of complicated bumping 
  2511  and retreating before arriving at a final retention register. Notably, 
  2512  ``bump and retreat'' can create a chain. If Employee A bumps Employee 
  2513  B, then Employee B is released from that competitive level, and the 
  2514  agency must determine whether Employee B has his or her own bump or 
  2515  retreat right. This process is highly burdensome and prone to errors.
  2516      This rule replaces the current rules with a streamlined system that 
  2517  eliminates the need for multiple, complicated rounds of bump and 
  2518  retreat, replacing it with a straightforward comparison of employee 
  2519  performance as augmented by veterans' preference, with ties broken by 
  2520  tenure and length of service. Further, OPM's new rules are simpler 
  2521  because they eliminate the most confusing features of the current 
  2522  rules: using performance to manufacture an adjusted service computation 
  2523  date and complicated bump-and-retreat procedures.
  2524      This rule addresses that problem by making performance credit more 
  2525  transparent and direct: Level 5 ratings receive 7 points, Level 4 
  2526  ratings receive 5 points, Level 3 ratings receive 3 points, and Level 1 
  2527  or 2 ratings receive no points. Veterans' preference is then added to 
  2528  that performance credit.
  2529      This rule's use of defined point values--Level 5 = 7 points, Level 
  2530  4 = 5 points, Level 3 = 3 points, and Level 1 or 2 = 0 points--also 
  2531  makes the RIF calculation easier to understand and audit than an 
  2532  artificial performance-adjusted SCD. As Commenter 0687 noted, this 
  2533  reform simplifies the composition of retention registers.
  2534      In addition, this rule does not change the basic record-keeping 
  2535  requirements in current Sec.  351.505 (renumbered to Sec.  351.506) or 
  2536  the notice requirements in Sec.  351.802, except to conform their

content.text:
Very useful: line 2496-2509 describes the current (prior) rules: tenure group I/II/III, then veterans' preference subgroup AD/A/B, then years of service as augmented by performance credit, earliest service date. So Q2(c): Bianchi (AD) above Abbott (B). ✓ And Q5(a): old rules — Lee's earlier SCD outranks Park's performance.

Also note Q13 candidate: line 2287-2290: "Competitive service tenure subgroup II will consist of every other competitive service employee who, as of the date of the RIF notice, is not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less." Text 351.502(a)(3) says "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316" — preamble says "temporary or term appointment." Hmm, that's a difference (category of appointment). Marginal but real: preamble includes "term" appointments in the exclusion for subgroup II, while the text excludes only temporary appointments of 1 year or less under subpart D. And the preamble at 1659-1662 (final rule changes) says they removed the proposed reference to term appointments. So another passage of the preamble states it correctly. Good Q13 item: 91 FR 49196 vs 49194/49191.

Also line 2309-2317: "an agency may establish a cut-off date after which no new rating of record will be considered" — consistent.

  2545  
  2546      In the proposed rule, OPM provided order of retention examples. 
  2547  Commenter 0680 points out correctly that some of the tables 
  2548  illustrating the operation of the proposed rule contained errors, as 
  2549  they incorrectly ranked employees in a higher tenure subgroup ahead of 
  2550  employees with a greater performance credit. OPM is therefore 
  2551  correcting these examples below. OPM is also publishing further 
  2552  examples of how retention standing will work under the new regulations 
  2553  to aid with administration of the new rules.
  2554      OPM disagrees with Commenter 0680 that these inadvertent errors 
  2555  show a lack of reasoned decision-making, that the new rules increase 
  2556  the risk of mistakes, or that OPM or agencies are unprepared to 
  2557  administer the new rules. Such a correction is consistent with ordinary 
  2558  rulemaking practice: agencies often revise, add, delete, or correct 
  2559  examples to conform them to the operative regulatory standard or to 
  2560  respond to comments.\16\ The binding rule is the regulatory text, which 
  2561  provides that employees are ranked by performance credit as augmented 
  2562  by veterans' preference, with tenure subgroup and service computation 
  2563  date used as tie-breakers. The proposed rule text clearly stated that, 
  2564  within each tenure group, employees are ranked by performance credit as 
  2565  augmented by veterans' preference, and only when employees have the 
  2566  same augmented performance credit are they further ranked by tenure 
  2567  subgroup and then by length of service.
  2568      Indeed, OPM believes the new RIF formula is much simpler to 
  2569  understand and apply than the current formula, as it involves a simple 
  2570  calculation of performance credits adjusted for veterans' status, with 
  2571  tenure subgroup and length of service serving as tiebreakers. The 
  2572  current system, by contrast, involves a multi-layered system where 
  2573  employees were sorted into three tenure groups, with veterans' status 
  2574  subgroups within each tenure group, with employees then further sorted 
  2575  by service computation date that is adjusted based on performance. That 
  2576  process required agencies to translate performance into years, average 
  2577  the credited years, round where necessary, and then move the employee's 
  2578  service date backward to create an ``adjusted SCD.'' That made the 
  2579  register harder to understand because the service computation date was 
  2580  not the employee's actual service date, but an artificial service date 
  2581  reflecting both service and performance. Further, agencies were then 
  2582  required to engage in complicated ``bump and retreat'' exercises 
  2583  between employees in different tenure groups, often encompassing 
  2584  multiple rounds of RIF competition governed by detailed rules that were 
  2585  understood by very few beyond a very small group of Federal HR 
  2586  specialists and consultants.
  2587      Under this rule, by contrast, performance remains a score that 
  2588  corresponds to direct numerical values, augmented by consistent 
  2589  numerical values for veterans' preference. Thus, the new rules will 
  2590  likely result in far fewer errors than the old rules. They are also 
  2591  easier and more streamlined, making them easier to apply and understand 
  2592  by both HR offices and Federal employees. Employees who inspect the 
  2593  register will be much more likely to understand how their retention 
  2594  standing was calculated and be able to spot errors.

Found an important Q13 candidate at line 2838-2843: "OPM is also modifying Sec. 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a competitive level while releasing a competing employee from that level." But the regulatory text of 351.602 (as revised) retains the prohibition: "(a) A specifically limited temporary or term promotion". Note the preamble says "temporary appointment," the text says "temporary or term promotion." Hmm — different category: preamble says "temporary appointment" removed prohibition; text prohibits retaining an employee with "a specifically limited temporary or term promotion". So the preamble mischaracterizes (appointment vs promotion). This is a good Q13 item, FR page 49202 vs 49223.

Also relevant to Q9 step 8: 351.602(a) prohibits releasing while retaining an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion → Reyes (temporary promotion ending March 2027) → noncompliant. ✓

Also note Q13: "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.601 for consistency..." fine.

Another: line 2807: "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.506(c) to make these provisions consistent with changes in Sec. 351.505" — but the correction 2026-17335 fixed (c)(2) citation. Not preamble vs text.

Continue reading 2877-3200 (subpart F rest, G, H).

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

  2960  mandatory exception to the ordinary RIF order of release. The agency 
  2961  must first determine the employee's ordinary retention standing under

  2964  the agency may not release a restoration protected employee from the

  2969  351.605. When an entire competitive area is abolished pursuant to Sec.  
  2970  351.605, the agency may not separate the restoration protected employee 
  2971  by RIF during the applicable 6-month or 1-year protection period. 
  2972  Instead, the employee must be assigned by the agency to a different

  2974  qualified, consistent with 5 CFR part 353.

  2977  an employee performing duty with the uniformed services may not be 
  2978  demoted or separated, other than military separation, except for cause; 
  2979  that RIF is not ``for cause'' under that subpart; that the employee is 
  2980  not a competing employee under part 351; and that, if the employee's 
  2981  position is abolished during the absence, the agency must reassign the 
  2982  employee to another position of like status and pay. OPM is clarifying 
  2983  that this reassignment obligation applies when the employee's position 
  2984  is abolished in a RIF, including when all positions in the employee's 
  2985  competitive area are abolished under Sec.  351.605.

  2990  restoration provisions in 5 CFR part 353. If the employing agency no 
  2991  longer exists and its functions have not been transferred, or if it is 
  2992  impossible or unreasonable for the agency to reassign the restoration 
  2993  protected employee, OPM will offer placement assistance elsewhere in 
  2994  the executive branch to the employee pursuant to 5 CFR 353.110.

  3003  6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period, the mandatory 
  3004  exception in Sec.  351.606(a) operates independently of the employee's 
  3005  ordinary retention standing. Thus, the employee is not penalized for 
  3006  lacking recent civilian ratings during the protected period; the agency 
  3007  must honor the USERRA retention protection before releasing the

  3051  
  3052      OPM is revising Sec.  351.701(a) to replace tenure groups I and II

  3054  changes in this rulemaking.
  3055      OPM is consolidating Sec.  351.701(b) and (c), simplifying the 
  3056  method of applying assignment rights. Based on the new method of 
  3057  defining tenure groups and assigning retention standing based on 
  3058  performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, with tenure 
  3059  subgroup and length of service as tiebreakers, subgroups will no longer

  3072  different subgroups.

  3076  that this restriction on employees with a current annual performance 
  3077  rating of record of Level 2 from obtaining assignment to positions held 
  3078  by employees with a higher performance rating is no longer necessary. 
  3079  OPM did not receive significant adverse comment on the removal of this

  3081      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.702(a)(4), pertaining to qualifications 
  3082  for assignment to a new position, to include language clarifying that 
  3083  in determining qualifications for reassignment an agency must use an 
  3084  assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related skills, 
  3085  abilities, knowledge, and competencies; is based on a job analysis; and 
  3086  does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination. 
  3087  Commenter 0687 supported this change, expressing ``appreciat[ion] that 
  3088  OPM has added a mechanism for agencies to utilize assessments to 
  3089  determine qualification for those assignments that is skills-based and 
  3090  consistent with merit principles in selection.''
  3091      On the other hand, Commenter 0685 expressed concern that the use of 
  3092  assessments would ``inject subjectivity into what has traditionally 
  3093  been a more mechanical qualification determination.'' OPM disagrees. 
  3094  The current rule provides that an employee is qualified for a position 
  3095  if the employee ``[h]as the capacity, adaptability, and special skills 
  3096  needed to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position without 
  3097  undue interruption,'' but provides no other guidance for making this 
  3098  determination, other than that an agency may consider ``recency of 
  3099  experience, when appropriate.'' OPM believes that the use of a 
  3100  validated assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related 
  3101  skills, abilities, knowledge, and competencies, such as a structured 
  3102  interview, structured resume review, or a work-related exercise, will 
  3103  reduce the subjectivity of making a qualifications determination, 
  3104  requiring that an employee demonstrate their job-related skills in a 
  3105  measured, objective fashion. In so doing, OPM is aligning qualification 
  3106  determinations for assignment in a RIF with otherwise-applicable merit-

  3111  
  3112      \17\ Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy & OPM, Merit

  3144  
  3145      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.802(a) to include the introductory

  3162  OPM is including the phrase ``Except as otherwise provided in this

  3167  required to build a retention register and must not apply assignment

  3170  substitute ``veterans' status'' for ``subgroup,'' and to add references

Good. Key items for Q6(e): line 3073-3080: OPM eliminated 351.701(d), the restriction on Level 2 employees; and eliminated bump/retreat (3055-3072). So the old HR handbook's statement is outdated: "bumping" and "retreating" replaced; Level 2 restriction removed.

Q13 candidates so far:
1. Erosion of duties: preamble says modifying 351.201(a)(2), with 180-day trigger; text amends 351.202(c)(3) with "adversely affect retention standing" trigger (49190 vs 49218/49219). Also repeated at 49191. Correct statement elsewhere? At 1576-1581 the preamble describes the actual standard correctly. Also executive summary item 8 correctly describes.
2. Subgroup II "temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less" (49196) vs text "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D" (49220); the preamble at 49191 (1659-1662) says the final rule removed the reference to term appointments.

5. Line 3032-3037: "(d) ... subject to a 90-day cap" — text (d)(4): period of retention does not exceed 90 days. Consistent.

7. Line 2888-2889: 351.605(c) notice content — text: (a)(1),(a)(3),(a)(5),(a)(6) and (b); not (a)(2) or (a)(4). [2026-15665: lines 439-738 of 6220, FR page 49181]
   439  B. The Rule Preserves Veterans' Preference as a Substantial Factor in 
   440  RIF Retention
   441  
   442      Many commenters (for example, 0005, 0660, 0672, 0680, and 0157) 
   443  criticized OPM's proposal because, in their view, the proposal 
   444  undermines veterans' preference. OPM disagrees. The relevant statute, 5 
   445  U.S.C. 3502, requires that preference eligibles under 5 U.S.C. 2108 
   446  receive preference in RIF retention, with 30-percent-or-more disabled 
   447  veterans receiving preference above other veterans. However, the 
   448  statute does not require the current regulatory subgroup structure and 
   449  does not forbid OPM from giving more weight to performance in RIF 
   450  retention.
   451      OPM gives veterans' preference due and substantial effect through 
   452  an explicit point augmentation that changes an employee's relative 
   453  standing in the retention register. The rule retains veterans' 
   454  preference as a meaningful part of retention standing by adding 5 
   455  points for preference eligibles with a compensable service-connected 
   456  disability of 30 percent or more and 3 points for other preference 
   457  eligibles. Those points are added to performance credit before tenure 
   458  subgroup and service computation date are considered. This level of 
   459  veterans' preference meaningfully honors veterans' sacrifice and 
   460  service \1\ while appropriately balancing the government's interest in 
   461  retaining top performers when an agency undergoes restructuring. This 
   462  rule thus gives effect to Congress's direction that disabled veterans 
   463  be retained ``in preference to'' other veterans, 5 U.S.C. 3502(b), and 
   464  that veterans be retained ``in preference to other competing 
   465  employees.'' 5 U.S.C. 3502(c).
   466  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   467  
   468      \1\ This rule also allows consideration for the sacrifice 
   469  endured by other categories of preference eligibles under 5 U.S.C. 
   470  2108(3), such as certain close family members of veterans.
   471  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   472  
   473      Notably, the amount of veterans' preference provided under these 
   474  provisions is much greater than the preference veterans receive in 
   475  competitive examining for hiring using numerical rating and ranking 
   476  under 5 U.S.C. 3309 and 5 CFR 337.101(a). Under these authorities, 
   477  disabled veterans receive an additional 10 points on a 100-point scale, 
   478  while veterans receive an extra 5 points on a 100-point scale. By 
   479  contrast, this rule adds 5 points (for disabled veterans) or 3 points 
   480  (for other preference eligibles) out of an ordinary maximum performance 
   481  credit score of 21. Thus, on a scale-normalized basis, veterans' 
   482  preference points in RIF retention are far greater than in typical 
   483  competitive hiring. This is illustrated by the chart below showing how 
   484  veterans' preference is applied in ordinary competitive examining with 
   485  numerical rating and ranking:
   486  
   487  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   488                                                                                                     Preference as
   489                     Hiring preference category                      Earned-rating    Preference    percent of 100-
   490                                                                         scale          points        point scale
   491  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   492  5-point preference eligible.....................................             100              +5               5
   493  10-point preference eligible....................................             100             +10              10
   494  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   495  
   496      Compare this to how RIF retention will work under the revised RIF 
   497  regulations:
   498  
   499  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   500                                                                                                     Preference as
   501                       RIF preference category                       Performance-     Preference    percent of 21-
   502                                                                     credit scale   percent points    point scale
   503  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   504  Other preference eligible, Subgroup A...........................              21              +3            14.3
   505  30%+ compensably disabled preference eligible, Subgroup AD......              21              +5            23.8
   506  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   507  
   508      Thus, the RIF preference can offset a much larger share of the 
   509  performance scale than hiring preference offsets of the examining 
   510  scale. In hiring, a 10-point preference eligible with an earned score 
   511  of 90 reaches an augmented score of 100. A 5-point preference eligible 
   512  with an earned score of 95 reaches an augmented score of 100. That 
   513  means hiring preference bridges the top 10% or 5% of the 100-point 
   514  earned-rating scale.
   515      Under this rule, a 30%+ disabled preference eligible with a raw 
   516  performance-credit score of 16 reaches 21 after the +5 preference 
   517  addition. Other preference eligibles with a raw performance-credit 
   518  score of 18 reach 21 after the +3 preference addition. Because the 
   519  maximum ordinary performance-credit score is 21, the RIF preference 
   520  bridges the top 23.8% or 14.3% of the performance-credit scale. That 
   521  makes the revised RIF veterans' preference materially stronger than 
   522  hiring preference as a scoring weight.
   523      Further, the practical effect of veterans' preference under this 
   524  rule is far greater than preference in competitive hiring, because RIF 
   525  performance-credit increments are relatively small. Under the new RIF 
   526  formula, the difference between a Level 5 rating and a Level 4 rating 
   527  is only 2
   528  
   529  [[Page 49182]]
   530  
   531  points, and the difference between a Level 4 rating and a Level 3 
   532  rating is also only 2 points. That means a +3 veterans' preference 
   533  credit is larger than one ordinary one-level rating difference, and a 
   534  +5 credit is larger than two ordinary one-level rating differences. For 
   535  example:
   536  
   537  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   538                                                                          Raw
   539                      Employee                          Ratings       performance      Veterans'     Augmented RIF
   540                                                                        credit        preference         score
   541  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   542  Non-preference employee.........................           5/5/4              19              +0              19
   543  30%+ disabled preference eligible...............           4/4/4              15              +5              20
   544  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   545  
   546      In this example, the 30%+ disabled preference eligible with three 
   547  Level 4 ratings ranks ahead of a non-preference employee with two Level 
   548  5 ratings and one Level 4 rating.
   549      Similarly:
   550  
   551  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   552                                                                          Raw
   553                      Employee                          Ratings       performance      Veterans'     Augmented RIF
   554                                                                        credit        preference         score
   555  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   556  Non-preference employee.........................           5/4/4              17              +0              17
   557  Other preference eligible.......................           4/4/4              15              +3              18
   558  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   559  
   560      In that example, the non-disabled preference eligible with three 
   561  Level 4 ratings ranks ahead of a non-preference employee with one Level 
   562  5 and two Level 4 ratings. These examples show that Commenter 0157's 
   563  contention that veterans' preference would be ``largely illusory'' 
   564  under these revised regulations is not accurate; instead, it provides 
   565  substantial retention preference for both disabled veterans and non-
   566  disabled veterans.
   567      OPM believes that veterans' preference under 5 U.S.C. 3502(b) and 
   568  (c) may lawfully be operationalized through a points-based addition to 
   569  performance credit. The statute provides that a preference eligible 
   570  employee with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent 
   571  or more whose performance has not been rated ``unacceptable'' is 
   572  entitled to retention preference ahead of other veterans. 5 U.S.C. 
   573  3502(b). Other preference eligibles whose performance has not been 
   574  rated ``unacceptable'' are entitled to retention ``in preference to 
   575  other competing employees.'' 5 U.S.C. 3502(c).
   576      Commenters 0660 and 0680 read 5 U.S.C. 3502(b) and (c) to mean that 
   577  a preference eligible whose performance is not unacceptable must always 
   578  be retained ahead of every non-preference eligible, regardless of 
   579  comparative performance. OPM disagrees. The statute does not require 
   580  that disabled veterans and other preference eligibles must always 
   581  appear first on the retention register, only that they be retained ``in 
   582  preference to'' other competing employees. These provisions create an 
   583  entitlement to a meaningful retention preference, not a categorical 
   584  right to be retained ahead of every non-veteran regardless of 
   585  performance.
   586      Further, sections 3502(b) and (c) must be read together with 
   587  section 3502(a). Subsection (a) requires OPM to issue regulations that 
   588  give ``due effect'' in a RIF not only to military preference, but also 
   589  to tenure, length of service, and performance ratings, without 
   590  establishing any categorical hierarchy concerning how the factors must 
   591  be applied.
   592      This lack of specific direction is notable, because Congress has 
   593  elsewhere directed specifically that disabled veterans with a 
   594  compensable service-connected disability of 10 percent or more ``be 
   595  entered on appropriate registers or list of eligibles'' before other 
   596  candidates for positions other than scientific and technical positions 
   597  in GS-9 or higher. 5 U.S.C. 3313; see also Legislative History of the 
   598  Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 at p. 789 (``Certain other disabled 
   599  veterans go to the top of the list of eligibles, except in competition 
   600  for professional and scientific positions in grade and [sic] GS-9 and 
   601  above''). This provision was codified at the same time as the modern 
   602  RIF statute. See Pub. L. 89-554, Sept. 6, 1966. Congress's use of much 
   603  more general language--``is entitled to be retained in preference to'' 
   604  other preference eligibles or competing employees, as applicable--in 
   605  the RIF statute, when contrasted with the specific direction in 5 
   606  U.S.C. 3313 that disabled veterans appear before other candidates on 
   607  hiring registers--indicates that Congress did not intend to create a 
   608  rigid structure under which disabled veterans or veterans must always 
   609  appear at the top of the retention register.
   610      As a further example, USERRA states expressly that veterans who are 
   611  required to be reemployed by their employers after a tour of duty in 
   612  the uniformed services ``shall not be discharged from such employment, 
   613  except for cause'' for periods of six months (for military service 
   614  between 30 days and 180 days) or one year (for military service of more 
   615  than 180 days). 38 U.S.C. 4316. This provision underscores that 
   616  Congress speaks directly when it means to give absolute retention 
   617  rights to certain groups of employees, as opposed to a preference.
   618      Indeed, OPM's current RIF regulations subordinate veterans' 
   619  preference to another factor, namely tenure. That is, employees are 
   620  currently ranked according to tenure groups I, II, III, and veterans 
   621  only enjoy preference ahead of other employees in their tenure group. 
   622  Thus, a veteran in tenure group II is ranked below a non-veteran in 
   623  tenure group I in retention standing.
   624      This longstanding feature of OPM's RIF regulations reflects the 
   625  fact that, in 5 U.S.C. 3502, Congress did not prescribe that veterans 
   626  or disabled veterans must always appear first on the register. As the 
   627  Director of the Civil Service Commission's Bureau of Recruitment and 
   628  Examining testified in 1977 concerning RIF regulations:
   629  
   630      In retention, veterans have the right to be retained over competing 
   631  non-veterans in a reduction in force. Retention standing under the law 
   632  is based on four factors: type of appointment, veterans preference, 
   633  performance rating, and length of service. Although this gives veterans 
   634  a significant advantage, it is not absolute. For example, in fiscal 
   635  year, 1976, 1800 veterans were separated in Reduction in Force actions 
   636  versus 3,000 nonveterans. An equal number of veterans and nonveterans 
   637  (approximately 4,500) were also reduced in grade. (quoted in
   638  
   639  [[Page 49183]]
   640  
   641  Legislative History of the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 at p. 789; 
   642  emphasis added)
   643  
   644      Under OPM's current RIF rules, a Group II preference eligible can 
   645  be released--and ultimately separated--before a Group I non-veteran, 
   646  even if the preference eligible has a stronger performance credit, as 
   647  in the example below (which assumes that both employees are in the same 
   648  competitive area and competitive level, one position is abolished, no 
   649  mandatory or permissive exception applies, and there is no position for 
   650  Employee B to bump or retreat to):
   651  
   652  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   653                                                                                                        Veterans'
   654                Rank                      Employee          Veteran status        Tenure group         preference       Adjusted SCD          Result
   655                                                                                                        subgroup
   656  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   657  1...............................  Employee A.........  Non-veteran........  Group I............  Subgroup B........      2002-01-01  Retained.
   658  2...............................  Employee B.........  30%+ disabled        Group II...........  Subgroup AD.......      1995-01-01  Released.
   659                                                          veteran.
   660  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   661  
   662      However, under this rule, the higher-performing preference eligible 
   663  may be retained over the longer-tenured non-veteran, as shown below:
   664  
   665  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   666                                                                                              Rating of                         Total
   667        Rank              Employee              Tenure group           Vets pref group     record summary     Vets pref      performance       Tenure            SCD                Result
   668                                                                                               levels          points          credit         subgroup
   669  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   670  1..............  Employee B............  CS....................  AD....................           5/5/5              +5              26              II      2024-01-01  Retained.
   671  2..............  Employee A............  CS....................  B.....................           4/5/4              +0              17               I      2015-01-01  Released.
   672  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   673  
   674      In this example, Employee B will fare better than Employee A 
   675  because the revised regulations no longer rank all Group I employees 
   676  ahead of all Group II employees. Instead, both will be placed in the 
   677  competitive-service tenure group, and Employee A's former Group I 
   678  status will function as tenure subgroup I, while Employee B's former 
   679  Group II status will function as tenure subgroup II. Tenure subgroup 
   680  would operate as a tie-breaker after performance credit, as augmented 
   681  by veterans' preference.
   682      In sum, this rule changes the method of operationalizing 
   683  preference, but not the underlying principle. Current rules 
   684  operationalize preference through categorical subgroups within tenure 
   685  groups. This final rule operationalizes preference through numerical 
   686  augmentation of performance credit. Both are regulatory methods for 
   687  giving effect to military preference within a multi-factor RIF system.
   688      Title 5 elsewhere confirms that veterans' preference can be 
   689  implemented through points. As noted above, in competitive examining, 5 
   690  U.S.C. 3309 provides that preference eligibles who receive passing 
   691  scores are entitled to additional points above their earned rating: 10 
   692  points for certain preference eligibles and 5 points for others. OPM's 
   693  regulation implements that provision on a 100-point examining scale, 
   694  adding 5 or 10 points to passing applicants' earned numerical ratings. 
   695  See 5 CFR 337.101(b).
   696      The general veterans' preference policy in 5 U.S.C. 1302(b) and (c) 
   697  states that preference shall be given in certification, appointment, 
   698  reinstatement, reemployment, and retention. OPM has discretion under 5 
   699  U.S.C. 1302(b) to ``prescribe and enforce regulations for the 
   700  administration of'' veterans' preference in the civil service. In the 
   701  examining context, Congress and OPM implement that preference through a 
   702  point credit, not an automatic selection entitlement. The same 
   703  conceptual approach is available in RIF retention unless the RIF 
   704  statute clearly forecloses it. Section 3502 does not. It requires due 
   705  effect to military preference and specifically grants a retention 
   706  preference, but it does not prescribe a fixed subgroup hierarchy or 
   707  prohibit OPM from implementing that preference through a substantial 
   708  numerical credit.
   709      Commenter 0532's example, in which a non-veteran with three 
   710  Outstanding ratings may rank above a disabled veteran with three Fully 
   711  Successful ratings, does not show that veterans' preference has been 
   712  erased. Instead, the example confirms that veterans' preference 
   713  operates as a significant preference within a performance-centered RIF 
   714  system rather than as an absolute rule that overrides all performance 
   715  distinctions. OPM considers that approach consistent with the statutory 
   716  direction to give due effect to all required factors.
   717      Commenter 0680 similarly offers an example in which a veteran with 
   718  ratings of 4/4/5 and 40 years of service receives 20 total points, 
   719  while a non-veteran with ratings of 5/5/5 and 4 years of service 
   720  receives 21 points. Commenter 0680 argues that the non-veteran's higher 
   721  ranking shows that veterans' preference has been unlawfully denied.
   722      OPM disagrees. The example shows only that, under the rule, a non-
   723  preference eligible with a materially stronger performance record may 
   724  rank ahead of a preference eligible in some circumstances. That is a 
   725  feature of a system designed to give meaningful effect to both 
   726  veterans' preference and performance, not evidence that veterans' 
   727  preference has been erased. The veteran in the commenters' example 
   728  receives an additional 3 points solely by virtue of preference status. 
   729  Without that preference, the veteran's performance score would be 17, 
   730  not 20. The preference therefore materially improves the veteran's 
   731  standing, but it does not operate as an absolute override of all higher 
   732  performance. It operationalizes Congress's direction that veterans be 
   733  retained ``in preference to other competing employees.'' 5 U.S.C. 
   734  3502(c).
   735  
   736  C. Giving Greater Weight to Performance in RIF Retention Standing is 
   737  Consistent With Merit-System Principles
   738

Very helpful for Q2(c) and Q5(a): current rules rank tenure group first, then vets subgroup (AD, A, B), then adjusted SCD (SCD adjusted for performance credit). So under old rules, a preference eligible in Group I AD outranks a non-veteran in Group I B regardless of performance. Bianchi (Group I, AD) vs Abbott (Group I, B) → Bianchi above. But wait: both career → Group I. Yes, Bianchi above Abbott under old rules because subgroup AD > B, before length of service/performance.

For Q5(a)(i) old rules: both Group I, subgroup B (no preference). Then adjusted SCD: SCD adjusted for performance credit. Lee: SCD 1998, ratings 3/3/3 (9 performance credit → old rule: performance credit = additional service credit; old rules: additional credit = years based on ratings). Lee's ASCD would be 1998 minus 9 years? In the example at line 2733: Kai with performance credit 12 years and SCD 2008-07-20 got adjusted SCD 1996-07-20 → 12 years subtracted. So Lee: 9 years credit → 1998-03-02 minus 9 = 1989-03-02. Park: 21 years credit → 2019-07-08 minus 21 = 1998-07-08. So Lee's ASCD (1989) earlier than Park's (1998) → Lee retained, Park released.

So under the earlier rules, Park (longer adjusted service date) is released. Interesting.

Let me double check the old formula: "Current performance service credit" values: in examples, e.g. 3/3/3 → 12 years; 5/4/5 → 20 years; 5/5/5 → 20 years? Example 4 Current Rules: Harper 5/5/5 → 20 years; Imani 5/4/4 → 18; Jorge 4/3/3 → 14; Kai 3/3/3 → 12; Lena 3/3/3 → 12. Hmm so old credit formula: some formula (351.504 old): additional credit = sum of (rating-based credits)? 5/5/5=20, 5/4/4=18, 4/3/3=14, 3/3/3=12. Let's infer: maybe credit per rating: 5→7? 7+7+7=21 no. Try formula: value = 4*(level) - 8? L5=12, L4=8, L3=4? 5/5/5 = 36 no.

Maybe old rule: additional service credit = average of ratings converted: e.g., 5→? Known old 5 CFR 351.504: "additional retention service credit" = 4 years for each rating of 5? Hmm: 5/5/5=20 → 6.67 each? 5/4/4=18; 4/3/3=14; 3/3/3=12. Differences: 5 vs 4 = 1 point each? 5/5/5 (20) vs 5/4/4 (18): difference 2 for two levels down → 1 per level. 5/4/4 (18) vs 4/3/3 (14): from (5,4,4) to (4,3,3) = 4 steps → 4 points. Consistent 1 point per level. 4/3/3 (14) vs 3/3/3 (12): 2 steps → 2 points. Consistent. So base at L3 = 4 per rating (12 total), each level above 3 adds 1 per rating, L2 would be 3? So credit = sum over ratings of (level + 1)? L3 → 4 = 3+1; L4 → 5 = 4+1; L5 → 6 = 5+1. Then 5/5/5 = 18, not 20. Hmm.

Try: credit = sum of (level) + something: 3+3+3=9 → 12 (so +3); 4+3+3=10 → 14 (+4); 5+4+4=13 → 18 (+5); 5+5+5=15 → 20 (+5). Hmm +3, +4, +5, +5. Not linear.

Alternative: old credit computed as average rating then multiplied? (3+3+3)/3=3 → 12 years = 4*3; (4+3+3)/3=3.33 → 14? 4*3.333=13.3, round to 14? (5+4+4)/3=4.33 → 18? 4*4.33=17.3 → 18? (5+5+5)/3=5 → 20 = 4*5. Yes! So credit = 4 × average rating, rounded up to nearest whole year. Check Lee: 3/3/3 → 12 years. Park: 5/5/5 → 20 years. 

So Lee: SCD 1998-03-02 − 12 years = 1986-03-02. Park: 2019-07-08 − 20 = 1999-07-08. Lee retained, Park released. ✓ (Note the doc says performance credit converted to years; consistent.)

I should cite the FR pages for old rule description: 91 FR 49181-49183 (lines 618-623, 644-681) and 49198/49200 examples showing ASCD calculation. Also 5 CFR 349? no.

Careful: the preamble says current rules rank by tenure group, then veterans' preference subgroup, then adjusted SCD. Good. But is the "additional service credit" also computed for the four-year/three ratings? The examples show 3 ratings used. Fine. For Q5(a)(i) I'll present arithmetic showing Lee's ASCD earlier than Park's, with the caveat that the exact old formula (4 × average summary level, rounded up) is inferred from the preamble examples, not stated as text. Hmm — Q5 says "For the earlier rules, use only what Federal Register documents say about them, and show the arithmetic." The preamble gives examples showing 3/3/3 = 12 years and 5/5/5 = 20 years. So I can use those exact values since Lee has 3/3/3 and Park 5/5/5! Great — no inference needed: 12 years and 20 years come directly from the examples.

So Lee ASCD = 1998-03-02 − 12 years = 1986-03-02; Park ASCD = 2019-07-08 − 20 years = 1999-07-08. Lee ranks ahead. ✓

Now, Q2(c): old rules — Bianchi (Group I AD) above Abbott (Group I B). Cite 91 FR 49181-82 and 49198.

Good. Now next: Q1(d) — "Which RIFs do the amended rules govern, and which stay under earlier rules? Where stated?" Answer: DATES paragraph 91 FR 49178, plus Implementation Considerations (lines 3395-3418). Let me read that quickly (24 lines) to see whether it says more (e.g., about RIFs in progress).

Then: Q1(e) — other 2026 final rules amending part 351 effective on/after Sept 2, 2026: 2026-21320 (admin leave; amends 351.806? effective Nov 18, not yet in force today) and possibly 2026-21316 (senior professional performance; effective Nov 18). Need to check if 2026-21316 amends part 351. Also 2026-15666 (RIF Appeals) amends part 351 — but that's the appeals rule, a separate final rule published 2026 (Aug 3), effective Sept 2 — it does amend part 351 (subpart I, 351.802(a)(6), 351.807(e)). Q1(e) says "every other final rule published in 2026, through today, that amends 5 CFR part 351 (not counting corrections) with effect on or after the main rule's effective date." So include 2026-15666 (same effective date Sept 2, so "on or after"), 2026-21320 (Nov 18), and 2026-21316 if it amends 351. Also 2026-13715 (Performance Appraisal, effective Aug 6) — before Sept 2, so excluded (but it amends 351? It was in the cfr 5:351 filter list. Its effective date Aug 6, 2026 → earlier, so exclude; worth mentioning).

content.text:
Need the full 351.806 text from 2026-21320 (lines 1889-1960ish). And also the current (pre-Nov 18) 351.806 text as it exists today — which is... existing 351.806 in CFR before this rule (not printed in 2026 docs except maybe quoted). Hmm, Q8(a) asks: "What does 5 CFR 351.806 say about an employee's status during the notice period? Give both the version that applies today and any version that has been adopted but is not yet in force, with the document and the date it takes effect."

The version that applies today: as amended by 2026-15665 (Aug 3) — but did the main rule amend 351.806? The main rule's amendatory instructions for subpart H: instruction 36 (351.802) and 37 (351.805). No 351.806. So today's 351.806 is the pre-existing one (from earlier CFR), which is not printed in these documents... unless the admin leave rule's preamble quotes the current version. The grep shows line 231 "It replaces the..." (page 65926). Let me read the admin leave rule's 351.806 preamble discussion (lines ~209-235) and the regulatory text (1889-1960). Also whether the current version is quoted in the proposed rule (2026-13073). Hmm.

Q8(c): "What does OPM say allowed administrative leave during a RIF notice period before the adopted text takes effect?" — maybe OPM says that under existing 351.806(b)/5 U.S.C. 6329? Let's read.

Let me read admin leave rule lines 200-240 and 1886-1960.

content.text:
Q8(c): "What does OPM say allowed administrative leave during a RIF notice period before the adopted text takes effect?" OPM says its policy guidance (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025, section D.1.b) already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date (91 FR 65925-65926). Also the current 351.806 presumably contains a duty-status rule with "when possible" and a paragraph (c) emergency provision. Do we have the current text? The preamble at 65933: "The final rule preserves the duty-status presumption with a minor change in terminology. Revised Sec. 351.806(a) provides that '[u]nder ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period.' The change from 'when possible' to 'under ordinary circumstances'..." So current 351.806(a) says "when possible". Also 65936: "an employee may not be placed on leave without pay without the employee's consent" — current (c). The full current text isn't printed in these documents. I should say: the version in force today (i.e., as it stood before Nov 18, 2026) is not printed in full in any 2026 FR document; the preamble describes that it said "when possible" in paragraph (a) and had an emergency lack-of-work-or-funds provision now at (c). And the main RIF rule (2026-15665) did not amend 351.806.

Wait — is that right? Let me confirm the main rule's Subpart H amendments: instructions 36 (351.802) and 37 (351.805) only. Yes.

Hmm, but then Q8(a)'s "version that applies today" — perhaps the answer is: today (Nov 14, 2026) 351.806 still reads as originally promulgated (pre-2026), with (a) "When possible, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period" and (b)/(c) provisions; and OPM's 2026 amendments to 351.806 take effect Nov 18, 2026 (2026-21320). Since the CFR isn't available, I can't give the exact current text; I'll describe what the preamble attributes to it ("when possible"; (c) emergency annual leave/LWOP/nonpay). Also the exception to annual leave in the current rule — 351.608(e) refers to 351.606(b).

Actually I should check the proposed rule 2026-13073 (June 29, 2026), which may quote the current 351.806. Let me grep it for "when possible" — cheap. Also for Q8(b): "companion leave provision" = new 630.1403(c)(10): "Administrative leave is appropriate... during a RIF notice period" — need the text of (c)(10) to see whether consent is required and whether there's a limit on duration. We didn't see (c) text (beyond line 2005). Let me read lines 2006-2030.

Also Q8(b): "is there a limit on how long this leave may last?" — 630.1403(a)(3) says brief/short periods usually not more than 1 workday but may exceed when in circumstances in (c). Hmm, (c)(10) may specify. Let's read.

content.text:
630.1403(c)(10): administrative leave during RIF notice period "when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests." No consent requirement, no explicit duration limit in (c)(10). But (a)(3) says administrative leave is for brief/short periods usually ≤1 workday, and longer may be approved in circumstances in (c). Also 351.806(b) (adopted) allows leave for all or part of the notice period when appropriate and consistent with part 630 subpart N — no consent requirement, no cap. Compare: 351.608(c) (Government obligation exception) prohibits use of administrative leave.

Q8(b): consent not needed (no consent requirement in either 351.806(b) or 630.1403(c)(10); consent is required only for LWOP under 351.806(c)). Duration: no express limit for RIF notice-period leave; but (a)(3) states brief/short periods usually not more than 1 workday except as in (c); (c)(9)/(11) extended periods subject to Governmentwide/agency limits. Hmm, for (c)(10) there's no stated cap.

Also is there a limit? OPM preamble might discuss; but I'll answer: no express duration limit; the leave runs for the notice period (between receipt of RIF notice and separation) at agency discretion; general (a)(3) guidance on brevity with (c) as exception.

Now Q8(d): Does administrative leave change retention standing, notice rights, or appeal rights? Preamble says provisions do not alter substantive/procedural RIF requirements (91 FR 65926); retention standing determined as of the date employee receives notice (351.507), regardless of duty status; notice period requirements in 351.801-351.806; appeal rights under subpart I unaffected. Good.

Now MSPB rule 2026-16456 — need its content re RIF appeals (Q14(iii), Q7(a)). Let me read its regulatory text and relevant preamble. Check TOC/length.
